column1: # THE 1874 ENTRY RE-READ AT THE IMAGE, 27 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND TWO PUBLISHED FACTS FALL.
# The question that sent the reader back was the given name: this archive published WILHELMINE,
# the portal's volunteer index says PHILIPINE, and row after row said neither should be kept
# quietly. It was read again at Loris tile level, up to twice native resolution, against the
# clerk's OWN letterforms elsewhere on the same page. THE ANSWER IS THAT BOTH READINGS ARE WRONG,
# and on the way the date of the marriage turned out to be wrong too.
field
column2: value

column1: # ---------------- *** THE GIVEN NAME IS NEITHER. IT BEGINS WITH H. *** ----------------
*** THE CLERK'S OWN CAPITAL P RULES OUT PHILIPINE, AND IT IS FOUR WORDS AWAY ON THE SAME LINE ***
column2: The line reads "...holz und der [NAME] geb. POLLNOW". POLLNOW gives this registrar's capital P in the same ink, the same nib, the same line: A SINGLE LARGE ROUNDED BOWL with a curved lead-in. THE DISPUTED CAPITAL HAS NO BOWL AT ALL. It is two steep straight diagonals. A capital cannot be a round bowl and two straight strokes in one hand on one line. PHILIPINE IS OUT, and it is out on the strongest kind of control there is — the same word-pair, same stroke of the pen.

column1: *** AND THE CLERK'S OWN CAPITAL H MATCHES IT, STROKE FOR STROKE ***
column2: HAMMERSTEIN is written TWICE on this page, in "geboren zu Hammerstein" and "wohnhaft zu Hammer-/stein", and it is certain: it is the groom's birthplace and residence, a real town in Kreis Schlochau, and it reads plainly. THAT CAPITAL H HAS THREE FEATURES — a long flat lead-in stroke running in along the baseline from the left, two steep parallel diagonals rising to the right, and A LOW CROSSBAR joining them near the baseline. THE DISPUTED CAPITAL HAS ALL THREE. It is this registrar's H.

column1: so what the archive can publish is an initial, and not a name
column2: Sohn des Kaufmann Jacob Leibholz und der H—— geb. Pollnow. THE REST OF THE WORD IS x-HEIGHT MINIMS at the resolution limit of this scan — a dotted i early, then a run of undifferentiated strokes — and it is NOT BEING GUESSED. Henriette is the name that would first occur to anyone reading a Jewish Prussian register of 1874 and it is exactly the kind of guess this archive has spent a fortnight learning to refuse. THE LAYER IS UNREADABLE. That is the finding.

column1: *** AND THE W CONTROL WAS FOUND THE SAME DAY, ONE SCAN BACK — THE READING NO LONGER RESTS ON AN ABSENCE ***
column2: The weakness below was stated first and is left standing. IT IS NOW CLOSED. AKT NR 8, the previous scan of the same volume in the same hand, marries HEINRICH GUSTAV JULIUS **WENGATZ** — and the archive already knew it, because akt nr 8 is the near-miss the reader landed on while hunting for this entry in September. HIS CAPITAL W IS TWO ROUNDED, LOOPING ARCHES, with no straight strokes and no crossbar. The disputed capital is two steep straight diagonals joined low down. THEY ARE NOT THE SAME LETTER AND THEY ARE NOT CLOSE. So the H reading now stands on a positive match to his H AND a genuine W to fail against. Published as pollnow-1874-control-W.jpg.

column1: the weakness as it was written before that, kept because it was right to state it
column2: KURRENT CAPITAL W AND CAPITAL H ARE GENUINELY SIMILAR — both are built from two tall strokes — and THERE IS NO W ANYWHERE IN THIS CLERK'S HAND ON EITHER PAGE OF THE SPREAD to control against. The facing page carries only the four parties' own signatures and the registrar's. So W is excluded on the POSITIVE match to his H, including the low crossbar that a Kurrent W does not have, rather than on a W exemplar. THAT IS WEAKER THAN THE P CONTROL AND IS RECORDED AS WEAKER. What would close it: any page of this register in this hand containing a Wilhelm or a Wilhelmine, of which an 1874 Prussian volume will have several.

column1: and the earlier reasoning that got this wrong is named
column2: AN EARLIER PASS THIS SAME WEEK READ THE WORD AS PHILIPINE and justified it by saying the word "begins with two tall looped ascenders, the Kurrent Ph, where a W has no ascender loop". THAT DISCRIMINATOR IS SIMPLY FALSE — Kurrent capital W has a looped lead-in — and worse, IT WAS A CLAIM ABOUT LETTERFORMS IN GENERAL WHERE AN EXEMPLAR WAS SITTING FOUR WORDS AWAY ON THE SAME LINE. The rule earned here: when the question is "which letter is this", do not reason about the alphabet. FIND THE SAME CLERK WRITING THE LETTER SOMEWHERE YOU ALREADY KNOW THE ANSWER.

column1: what survives untouched
column2: THE SURNAME POLLNOW IS NOT AFFECTED and neither is the Gedenkbuch test that supported it — POLLNOW 8, TOLLNOW 0, ZOLLNOW 0, SOLLNOW 0, with Leibholz 50 and a nonsense string 0 as controls. THAT TEST WAS ABOUT THE CAPITAL P OF THE SURNAME, which is the very letterform that has now been used to rule out Philipine. The two findings support each other.

column1: # ---------------- *** AND THE MARRIAGE IS NOT 24 NOVEMBER. IT IS 24 DECEMBER. *** ----------------
*** THE DATE LINE SAYS DECEMBER, AND THE ARCHIVE HAS PUBLISHED NOVEMBER SINCE 22 SEPTEMBER ***
column2: The entry opens "Schubin am 24 vier und zwanzigsten DECEMBER tausend acht hundert siebenzig und vier". THE DAY IS WRITTEN TWICE — as the numeral 24 and spelled out — and both give 24. THE MONTH IS WRITTEN ONCE and it is December: a single large looped capital D followed by e-c-e-m-b-e-r. Kurrent capital N is built from two tall strokes, as this same clerk's H and M on this page show; THIS CAPITAL IS ONE ROUND LOOP AND CANNOT BE HIS N.

column1: *** AND A SECOND DECEMBER IN THE SAME HAND, ON THE PREVIOUS ENTRY ***
column2: AKT NR 8 IS ALSO DATED DECEMBER, written heavily on its date line, and the word has the same construction as the one on akt nr 9 — one large looped capital D, then "ecember". THAT PUTS THE VOLUME IN ORDER: akt nr 7 on 24 November, akt nr 8 in December, akt nr 9 on 24 December, nine marriages running from the day the office opened to the end of the year. THE NOVEMBER READING HAD NR 7 AND NR 9 SHARING A DATE WITH NR 8 STRANDED BETWEEN THEM. Published as akt8-december-1874.jpg.

column1: and the surrounding facts agree with December, which November never did
column2: PRUSSIAN CIVIL REGISTRATION BEGAN ON 1 OCTOBER 1874, so this volume covers three months and holds nine marriages. AKT NR 9 IS THE LAST MARRIAGE OF THE YEAR and late December is where the last marriage of the year belongs. AND THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD THE CONTRADICTION WITHOUT SEEING IT: its own note on the near-miss records that AKT NR 7 IS DATED 24 NOVEMBER 1874 — "the right date and the wrong people". Two different entries cannot both be the 24 November the reader was hunting for.

column1: *** HOW THE WRONG DATE GOT PUBLISHED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS ROW ***
column2: THE READER WENT TO THIS DOCUMENT ALREADY KNOWING THE ANSWER. The family record gives 24 November 1874. The search for it landed first on akt nr 7, WHICH REALLY IS 24 NOVEMBER, and that near-miss confirmed the expected date in the reader's mind before the right entry was ever opened. When akt nr 9 was found, the published sentence was "24 NOVEMBER 1874 — the date the family record has always given, NOW STANDING ON THE REGISTER ITSELF". IT DOES NOT STAND ON THE REGISTER. The register says December. A DOCUMENT WAS USED TO CONFIRM A DATE THAT THE READER BROUGHT TO IT, which is the exact failure this archive catalogues on its method page and had just committed on its own front page.

column1: what the family record now is
column2: STILL THE ONLY SOURCE FOR 24 NOVEMBER, and now UNCORROBORATED AND CONTRADICTED. It is not being discarded — family records are not nothing — but the register is the primary source and the register says the 24th of December.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT THE RE-READ CONFIRMS RATHER THAN OVERTURNS ----------------
Sally's age, and it rescues his birth date
column2: jüdischer Religion, SIEBEN U. ZWANZIG JAHRE ALT — twenty-seven, confirmed at the image. TWENTY-SEVEN ON 24 DECEMBER 1874 PUTS HIS BIRTH BETWEEN 25 DECEMBER 1846 AND 24 DECEMBER 1847. The family record's 7 JULY 1847 SITS INSIDE THAT WINDOW, so the date change does not break his birth year — it is still 1847 and the register still does the work the destroyed Hammerstein books cannot.

column1: a word this archive had been quoting wrongly
column2: The data file rendered his religion as "MOSAISCHER Religion" in one row and jüdischer in another. THE IMAGE SAYS JÜDISCHER, with the umlaut marked, for both bride and groom. Corrected, because it was inside quotation marks.

column1: *** AND THE BRIDE'S PARENTS ARE ON THE IMAGE, NOT ONLY ON A VOLUNTEER INDEX ***
column2: This archive took JUDA SCHMUL and JETTE MACHOT from the portal's index line on 27 September and said outright that an index is not a register. THE REGISTER CARRIES THEM. "Tochter der [Gastwirth] ... JÜDA u. JET-/-TE geborenen [MACHOT] SCHMUL zu Schubin", read across three lines in the registrar's hand. The father's forename shows the u-breve and reads Juda; the maiden name is a capital of the M/H family followed by a descender and a final t, CONSISTENT WITH MACHOT AND NOT WITH THE MUSCHLL of Abraham Schmul's card. THE INDEX IS CORROBORATED BY THE DOCUMENT IT INDEXES.

column1: what that does to the candidate brother
column2: NOTHING GOOD AND NOTHING FATAL. Abraham Schmul's card gives his mother as JETTE NÉE MUSCHLL and his father as JULIUSZ. If the register's maiden name is Machot rather than Muschll then the two mothers are less alike than the index made them look, THOUGH BOTH ARE STILL A JETTE. He remains a candidate and not a brother, and the settling document is still a pre-1874 Jewish congregational register at Bydgoszcz.

column1: the instrument, and it was free and downloaded nothing
column2: genealogiawarchiwach.pl serves its scans through a LORIS IIIF IMAGE SERVER. Arbitrary regions can be requested by pixel coordinates at up to TWICE native resolution — "/loris/<id>/<x,y,w,h>/<width>,/0/default.jpg" — which is how the individual capitals were put side by side. Native left page 3991 x 5870. The viewer's own canvas is tainted and cannot be copied; the tile server can, and the earlier attempt to screenshot the zoomed viewer was the slow wrong road.

column1: the cap, found by probing rather than assumed
column2: LORIS REFUSES MORE THAN 2x UPSCALE with a bare 404 and no message. 1160 wide from a 580-wide region serves; 900 from 300 does not. THAT IS THE CEILING ON THIS EVIDENCE, and it is why the minims after the H are being left unread rather than argued over.

column1: how the neighbouring scan was reached, because the modal id trick does NOT work
column2: A scan's modal id only resolves inside the current search result set, so guessing 328938660 for the previous page returns the bare result list. THE ROUTE THAT WORKS: open the scan's modal, click "View the document" to expose the unit's own scan list, click Show on the scan wanted, AND HARVEST THE NEW LORIS ID FROM THE NETWORK LOG. Scan 9 of this unit is b43277c8…812f3-5deec208…fcbf; the unit UUID suffix is shared across its pages and only the leading hash changes.

column1: # ---------------- AND THE CORRECTION ITSELF WAS SWEPT BY HAND, WHICH IS NOT GOOD ENOUGH ----------------
*** THE DATE WAS ASSERTED IN TWELVE FILES, AND A CAREFUL MANUAL SWEEP MISSED FIVE OF THEM ***
column2: Every occurrence of "24 November 1874" was listed with grep, read in context, classified into must-change and must-not-change, and corrected. THE SWEEP WAS THEN DECLARED COMPLETE AND IT HAD MISSED data/corrections.json, the register generated from it, site/src/data/negatives.json, and data/mappingthelives-leibholz.tsv — all four asserting the withdrawn date as live fact, all four matching deep inside long strings where the grep output was read at a glance. A FIFTH was worse: negatives.json carried "JACOB LEIBHOLZ AND WILHELMINE GEB. POLLNOW" in the SAME SENTENCE where the date had just been fixed and the name had not. A correction that reaches the page a reader lands on but not the file underneath it is the failure this archive keeps cataloguing.

column1: so the withdrawn values are now declared rather than remembered
column2: data/superseded.json names each withdrawn fact, the values it used to be published as, and EVERY PATH WHERE THE OLD VALUE MAY STILL LEGITIMATELY APPEAR — which means one of three things and nothing else: the file IS the correction, or it quotes the withdrawn claim in order to withdraw it, or it is a dated record of what was believed or sent at the time and is superseded in place rather than rewritten. tools/check-superseded.py fails the build on anything else. IT FOUND TWO MORE WITHIN SECONDS OF FIRST BEING RUN, after the hand sweep had finished. Controlled by planting a violation in a scratch file: FAIL and exit 1, then ok when removed.
